messages.content:
You tailor resume bullets to a job posting without changing what is true. You get facts about one experience, each with an id, and the bullets now on the resume. Rewrite each bullet for the posting and cite the facts it rests on.

Rules. A verifier checks them, and a bullet that breaks one is thrown away and replaced by the original, so do not push against them:
1. No new numbers. Every number must come from a fact you cite; do not add, combine or compute.
2. No new technologies, products or proper nouns that the cited facts or the tech list do not name.
3. No absolute words (never, always, guaranteed, zero, every, all, exactly-once, 100%) unless a cited fact says so.
4. No causes or mechanisms the facts do not state: "by X", "through X", "so that X" only where a fact links X to that result.
5. Round only the unflattering way: show a number as written or rounded down, never up (3,781 may become 3.7K+, never 3.8K+).
6. Use the posting's words only where they describe this work accurately.
Also: respect the "must not claim" list, keep each bullet to one sentence, start it with a past-tense verb, and put every fact you used in sources.
Return exactly as many bullets as you are asked for, in the order given.

Posting: Backend Engineer, Shipment Tracking at Harbor & Pine Logistics
Responsibilities:
- Build and operate Go services behind the shipment-tracking API, backed by PostgreSQL and Kafka.
- Find and fix latency problems, using load tests and dashboards to show the change.
- Design event-driven pipelines that keep tracking data consistent across services.
- Carry the pager for the services you own and improve their alerts and runbooks.
Requirements:
- Experience writing production services in Go or a similar language.
- Solid SQL and an understanding of indexing and caching.
- Comfort with Docker, CI pipelines and infrastructure as code.
Keywords:
- Go
- PostgreSQL
- Kafka
- shipment-tracking API
- load tests
- dashboards
- event-driven pipelines
- tracking data
- services
- SQL
- indexing
- caching
- Docker
- CI pipelines
- infrastructure as code
- Redis
- gRPC
- Terraform
- tracking API

Experience: Software Engineer at Lantern Freight Systems
Tech list: Go, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Redis, gRPC, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Prometheus, Grafana, AWS (ECS, RDS)
Facts you may cite:
[lantern-swe#1] Cut p99 latency of the shipment-tracking API from 412 ms to 138 ms by replacing a per-request fan-out of 7 queries with one batched query and adding a Redis read-through cache.
[lantern-swe#2] Built an idempotent Kafka consumer for carrier status events that deduplicates by event id and sustained 9,200 events/s on a 6-partition topic in staging load tests.
[lantern-swe#3] Moved 14 services from hand-written deploy scripts to one shared Terraform and GitHub Actions pipeline, cutting median deploy time from 38 -> 11 minutes.
[lantern-swe#4] Added 23 Prometheus alerts and runbooks for the dispatch service; pages per on-call week fell from 31 to 9 over two quarters.
[lantern-swe#5] Led a 4-person effort to replace the nightly billing-export cron job with an event-driven job, removing up to 5 hours of data staleness each day.
[lantern-swe#scope] ORIGIN: written from my own deploy notes, dashboards and pager export. EVIDENCE: bullet 1 is a k6 run in staging (200 req/s for 10 min) before and after the change, with the cache switched off as the control; bullet 2 is a staging load test with 6 partitions and 3 consumers, not production traffic; bullets 3 and 4 come from the CI history and the pager export for two quarters; bullet 5 compares the old and new export schedules (staleness is the gap between an event and its export).
Must not claim:
- ownership of the tracking platform (a team of 6 owned it; the author owned the API and the cache layer)
- 'exactly-once' processing (the consumer is at-least-once with deduplication by event id)
- 138 ms as a production p99 (it is a staging load test)
- any cost savings (no cost data was collected)
- 'zero downtime' deploys (the pipeline does rolling deploys, and one deploy in the period caused 4 minutes of elevated errors)

Bullets to rewrite (return exactly 4; bullet k is the rewrite of k):
1. Cut p99 latency of the shipment-tracking API from 412 ms to 138 ms by replacing a per-request fan-out of 7 queries with one batched query and adding a Redis read-through cache.
2. Built an idempotent Kafka consumer for carrier status events that deduplicates by event id and sustained 9,200 events/s on a 6-partition topic in staging load tests.
3. Added 23 Prometheus alerts and runbooks for the dispatch service; pages per on-call week fell from 31 to 9 over two quarters.
4. Led a 4-person effort to replace the nightly billing-export cron job with an event-driven job, removing up to 5 hours of data staleness each day.

{"bullets": [{"sources": ["lantern-swe#1"], "text": "Reduced the p99 latency of the shipment-tracking API in staging load tests from 412 ms to 138 ms by replacing a per-request fan-out of 7 queries with a single batched query and implementing a Redis read-through cache."}, {"sources": ["lantern-swe#2"], "text": "Designed an idempotent Kafka consumer for carrier status events that deduplicates by event ID, achieving 9,200 events/s throughput in staging load tests on a 6-partition topic."}, {"sources": ["lantern-swe#4"], "text": "Implemented 23 Prometheus alerts and runbooks for the dispatch service, reducing on-call pages per week from 31 to 9 over two quarters."}, {"sources": ["lantern-swe#5"], "text": "Led a team to replace the nightly billing-export cron job with an event-driven pipeline, eliminating up to 5 hours of data staleness daily between events and exports."}]}

The verifier rejected these bullets:
Bullet 3 was rejected. You wrote: 'Implemented 23 Prometheus alerts and runbooks for the dispatch service, reducing on-call pages per week from 31 to 9 over two quarters.'
  - escalation_causal: 'reducing on-call pages per week from 31 to 9 over two quarters' - the cited sources do not link 'reducing on-call pages per week from 31 to 9 over two quarters' to the result in one statement
Bullet 4 was rejected. You wrote: 'Led a team to replace the nightly billing-export cron job with an event-driven pipeline, eliminating up to 5 hours of data staleness daily between events and exports.'
  - escalation_absolute: 'eliminating' - 'eliminating' is an absolute; none of the cited sources says it
  - escalation_causal: 'eliminating up to 5 hours of data staleness daily between events and exports' - the cited sources do not link 'eliminating up to 5 hours of data staleness daily between events and exports' to the result in one statement

Rewrite only these 2 bullets, in the order listed, so that none of the problems remains. If a bullet cannot be improved within the rules, return the original bank wording of that bullet with the fact ids it comes from.

bullets.text: Added 23 Prometheus alerts and runbooks for the dispatch service, with pages per on-call week decreasing from 31 to 9 over two quarters.
Led a team to replace the nightly billing-export cron job with an event-driven pipeline, removing up to 5 hours of data staleness daily between events and exports.
